key_insight: A cross-cohort machine learning model can identify early-stage node-negative breast cancer patients at higher relapse risk using clinical and cohort data, without relying on gene expression inputs.
clinical_relevance: If externally validated, this approach could help distinguish patients who may need chemotherapy from those likely to do well with endocrine therapy alone, reducing over- and undertreatment.
method: Trained and tested models on MSK-IMPACT and METABRIC breast cancer cohorts in both directions.
Evaluated five-fold cross-validation on the combined cohort to assess overall performance.
Used survival analysis, SHAP interpretability, and ablation testing to check clinical relevance and feature contributions.
evidence_signal: The combined cohort model reached AUC 0.788±0.028, with cross-cohort AUCs of 0.741 and 0.714, and out-of-fold METABRIC validation showed strong survival separation (DFS HR 3.01; OS HR 2.35).
watch_item: Performance may still vary across institutions, patient populations, and data preprocessing pipelines, so prospective validation is needed before clinical use.
paper_title: Cross-cohort generalizability of machine learning models for early-stage node-negative breast cancer relapse prediction
